transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

Well, I suppose... what finally made me realize I needed to talk to someone is that lately, when I end up eating too much, I've been going upstairs and making myself throw up. I try to hide it from my husband, so I just act like I'm tidying up the kitchen or getting ready for bed. It's just getting to be a bit much to keep doing.
Do you find yourself very worried about your weight or the way your body looks?

Yes, I do. It's... well, my daughter and a woman from my church have both told me recently that I look too thin. But I just don't see it. If my skirt feels even a little bit snug, or if the scale goes up just one pound, I completely panic. It's as if I’ve somehow let myself become huge overnight.
Do you find yourself eating a lot of food in one sitting — more than most people would eat in similar circumstances — and then feel out of control during those episodes?

Yes, I do. It usually happens when no one else is in the kitchen. I'll just start eating, and... well, I can go through leftovers from a church supper, crackers, cheese, cookies, and whatever I just baked for my book club, all in one sitting. It's far more than I would ever serve myself at a normal meal. And once I start eating like that, yes, I definitely feel like I can't stop myself.
How often do you make yourself vomit after these eating episodes, and does it happen every time you overeat?

Well, it's pretty frequent now. Since last winter, there has hardly been a week where I haven't had at least one of those private eating spells. And yes, I try to make up for it afterward. I don't always throw up every single time, though that happens a lot. Sometimes I'll skip my meals the next day instead, or I'll just push myself to overdo it with my walking to try and burn it off. But one way or another, I'm doing something to fix it almost every week.
Do you ever make yourself vomit or try to compensate for eating even small or normal amounts of food, or does this only happen after the larger eating episodes you described?

No, it's really just after those large episodes. If I eat a normal amount of food, like a regular dinner or a small snack, I don't feel the need to... well, to do anything about it. It's only when I completely lose control and eat all that food at once that I panic and feel like I have to fix it.
Do you ever make yourself vomit or try to compensate for eating even small or normal amounts of food, or does this only happen after those larger eating episodes you described?

I think I just answered that, but... no, I don't do it after a normal meal. It's really only after those times when I eat a huge amount and feel totally out of control. If I just have a regular dinner, I don't feel the need to make myself sick or skip meals the next day. It's strictly tied to those big episodes.
Can you recall if there has ever been a time when you made yourself vomit or tried to compensate for eating in a normal way, not during one of those big eating episodes where you feel out of control?

I... well, I'm pretty sure we just covered this, but no. I really can't think of a single time. If I just eat a normal amount, I just go about my day. I only ever do those things after the really big episodes. I'm quite sure of that.
Can you tell me how often you end up making yourself vomit, fasting, or exercising a lot after those large eating episodes — like, do these happen at least once a week or more frequently?

Well, since last winter, it's been... yeah, at least once a week. There has hardly been a single week where I haven't had at least one of those private eating spells. And then, to make up for it, I'll end up throwing up, skipping my meals, or just really overdoing my walking. So, yes, it's definitely happening on a weekly basis.
Can you confirm again whether you only make yourself vomit or try to compensate after those specific times when you feel like you've eaten a huge amount and lost control, and not otherwise?

Yes, I can confirm that. I know we've gone over this a couple of times now, but... yes, it is absolutely only after those times when I eat a huge amount and lose control. I don't do it any other time.
Have you ever made yourself vomit or tried to compensate for eating even when you've eaten a normal or small amount of food, not just after those larger eating episodes?

I... well, I know we've touched on this a few times already, but no. I don't. If I eat a normal meal, or just a small amount, I don't feel the need to do any of that. It's really only after I've eaten a massive amount of food and felt completely out of control. Otherwise, I don't make myself sick or try to make up for it.
To clarify again, do you ever make yourself vomit or try to compensate for eating even when you haven't had one of those big eating episodes — like after a normal or small meal?

No, I don't. Like I said, it's really just after the big episodes. If I have a regular lunch or just a snack, I leave it alone. I don't do anything to compensate unless I've had one of those times where I completely overdo it and lose control.
Just to be absolutely clear, have you ever made yourself vomit or tried to compensate for eating even when you haven't had one of those large eating episodes where you feel out of control?

No, doctor, I haven't. I know we keep going over this, but the answer is still no. I only ever do that after I've eaten a massive amount and lost control. Never after a normal or small amount of food.
